newsitem.title: USA: Peru power sector needs $300 mln a year to 2000.
newsitem.headline: Peru power sector needs $300 mln a year to 2000.

text.p: Peru's power sector will need $300 million to $350 million a year in investment through 2000 to meet rapidly growing electricity demand, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said.

"Power demand increases are being driven by population and economic growth, along with expansion of the country's mining sector, which is relatively energy-intensive," the agency said in an analysis released Friday of Peru's energy sector.
Peru currently has 4,520 megawatts of power generation capacity, of which more than half is hydroelectric.

Several new power projects are expected to help fill the rising demand, including a 600 megawatt, $500 million power plant due to start operating in 1999, which will use natural gas from the giant Camisea field.
Israel's Energy Horizons is considering building a 1,200 MW coal-fired plant near Salaverry on Peru's northern coast.

"If built, the plant ... would provide an alternative source of power to the deteriorating 1,000-megawatt Mantaro hydroelectric complex, which produces as much as 40 percent of Peru's electricity, and which is scheduled for privatization in 1997," the report said.

EIA said that oil exploration in Peru was "expected to surge, especially in the northern an southern jungle areas, over the next 2-3 years," with oil companies having committed $1.3 billion to drill in those areas.

Production from the Camisea field, due to pump between 250 million and 400 million cubic feet a day of gas and 70,000 barrels per day of condensates, is expected to turn Peru into a net exporter of hydrocarbons early in the next decade.
